claim.quote: This observation, which has a significance of 5.9 standard deviations, corresponding to a background fluctuation probability of 1.7x10^-9, is compatible with the production and decay of the Standard Model Higgs boson.

name: Observation of a new particle in the search for the Standard Model Higgs boson
notes: Collaboration wording is "observation of a new particle", not "discovery of the Higgs boson"; the identification with the Standard Model Higgs boson was established by later analyses (see result:atlas-nature-higgs-2022).
ATLAS announced the result publicly on 4 July 2012; the cited arXiv preprint was submitted 31 July 2012 and published as Phys. Lett. B 716 (2012) 1.

significance.quote: a significance of 5.9 standard deviations, corresponding to a background fluctuation probability of 1.7x10^-9

summary.plain: On 4 July 2012, ATLAS announced it had found a new particle weighing about 126 times as much as a proton. The collaboration was careful to call it 'a new particle', not yet 'the Higgs boson' - that identification came with later data.
summary.technical: Combined search in the gamma-gamma, ZZ* and WW* channels using up to 4.8 fb^-1 at 7 TeV and 5.8 fb^-1 at 8 TeV: local significance 5.9 sigma at m = 126.0 +/- 0.4 (stat.) +/- 0.4 (sys.) GeV, compatible with the Standard Model Higgs boson.

title: Observation of a new particle in the search for the Standard Model Higgs boson with the ATLAS detector at the LHC
why_it_matters: This was the observation that completed the Standard Model's particle content, announced jointly with CMS on 4 July 2012 and the starting point of a decade of precision Higgs measurements.
